note: Study checklists removed at your request.

items.title: Science asks for leftover craft supplies at the start of next week
items.detail: Optional. The space unit has started and students build a scaled model of the solar system in class from 6 Oct. Mrs. DiPietro wants pom poms, pipe cleaners, glue gun sticks, Elmer's glue, sticky dots, beads, wooden beads, styrofoam balls, whatever is already in the house. Part bags are fine. Sending it Monday matters because they plan their projects Tuesday and Wednesday around what has come in. Monday is already the book fair class visit, so both go in the bag together.

items.title: Scholastic Book Fair, 5 to 9 Oct, English class visits Monday
items.detail: Her English class goes to the fair together on Monday 5 Oct during the regular period, so if she is buying anything she needs money or a set up eWallet that morning, not later in the week. Cash, card, Apple Pay, checks to Watson Mountain Middle School, or a Scholastic eWallet all work. Parents can shop any time during school hours that week, and Friday 9 Oct is Bring Your Parent to School Day.

items.title: Monday: headphones for US History, and no violin
items.detail: Two things for the bag tomorrow morning. Mr. Dickerson is at the district office and the class works independently, so he asked students to bring their own headphones; he has a class set but says personal ones work better. Separately, Ms. Holowecki says Strings is doing a written music assignment tomorrow and instruments stay home. The violin goes back in on Wednesday.
items.source: Jeb Dickerson and Kelly Holowecki, 27 Sep

items.title: Fall chocolate fundraiser, 22 Sep to 13 Oct, fully optional
items.detail: World's Finest Chocolate, 40 bars at 2 dollars each, 80 dollars a box prepaid, plus a 3.30 fee if paid online. Once a box is checked out it cannot be returned, so the 80 dollars is at risk if it does not sell. Boxes are handed out from the auditorium at 8:30 am and are supposed to live in her locker until dismissal, which matters on B days when the violin is already in there. Selling one box gets her into a magic show. No signature needed, an online purchase is the permission.

items.title: Instrumental posture graded in Strings next week, shoulder rest needed
items.detail: Ms. Holowecki wrote on 17 Sep that every sixth grader gets an Instrumental Posture grade in class next week, and that violins and violas need their own shoulder rest for the posture to be right. She asked families to buy one as soon as possible. Suggestions are on page 3 of the Strings Handbook. Her class is on B days, so the first chance is Tuesday 22 Sep.

items.title: She is in Teal 6 Strings, four concert dates for the family calendar
items.detail: Strings 6 splits into two ensembles so the auditorium fits everyone. Her block, 4B, is Teal. Rehearsal Thursday 21 Jan 2027, 3:50 to 4:50 pm at school. Winter concert Thursday 28 Jan 2027, report 6:30 pm and perform 7:00 pm, later than the Red group the same night. Rehearsal Tuesday 18 May 2027, 3:50 to 4:50 pm. Spring concert Thursday 20 May 2027, report 6:30 pm and perform 7:00 pm. Both rehearsals end after the normal day, so they need a pickup plan. The same email lists private lesson instructors on the last page of the Strings Handbook if that is ever of interest.

items.title: 2028-29 school calendar, comment before the 22 Sep board vote
items.detail: Optional. LCPS reopened comment because board members proposed revisions and new options since the last round. The School Board votes Tuesday 22 Sep. LCPS has since put up a page with the options actually on the table plus an Onflo form that sends comments straight to the members. Adi would be in 8th grade that year.

items.title: 2027 to 2032 strategic plan, ThoughtExchange open to 1 Oct
items.detail: Optional. Dr. Spence opened the draft goals and strategies for the next five year LCPS plan to families. You share your own view and rate other people's ideas. Open 16 Sep to 1 Oct. A separate ThoughtExchange on the grading policy, including retake ceilings and extra credit, is due later this fall and is the one more likely to touch her day to day.

items.title: Intramurals and after school clubs start this week
items.detail: Posted to the Grade 6 course on Monday morning by Kjersti Oliver. Any day she stays after school she has to fill in the After School Attendance Form herself, once per day. Pickup is either a parent run or one of the two 5:00 pm activity buses, and the bus number and stop are on the 2026-2027 activity bus route sheet. Worth settling which bus she is on before the first day she stays.

items.title: Mr. Dickerson weekly update, content is in the attached PDF
items.detail: US History weekly note, sent late Friday night. The email body is empty and everything sits in an attached PDF, this one named 9-14-26.pdf, so it covers the week of 14 Sep. Same pattern every week, and the attachment cannot be read from here, so open it from the email if you want the detail.
items.source: Jeb Dickerson, US History to 1865 6H, 19 Sep

items.title: Substance abuse presentation in PE, opt out form attached
items.detail: Mrs. Allen wrote on 11 Sep that all sixth graders sit a Substance Abuse Presentation on 27 or 28 October during their normal PE period. An opt out document is attached to her email, so the decision is yours and the form goes back to her. No deadline was given, which usually means before the week of the presentation. Worth opening the attachment now rather than in late October.

items.title: Our Turn to Talk, parent and teen film night, 24 Sep
items.detail: Optional. A film following five teenagers on mental health and growing up, then a facilitated discussion. Thursday 24 Sep, 6 to 8 pm at the LCPS Administration Building in Ashburn. Food at 6, film at 6:30. Recommended for ages 12 and up, so she is on the edge of it. Registration required.

items.title: Gifted evaluation window, probably not needed for her
items.detail: LCPS opened the fall evaluation cycle for grades 6 to 8. The Permission to Evaluate form is due Friday 25 Sep and late forms are refused, though sixth and seventh graders get another cycle in January 2027. She is already scheduled in Spectrum 6 with Mrs. Cumberledge, which is the identified gifted programme, so this almost certainly does not apply to her. One question to the school gifted resource teacher settles it. Form link sits on the LCPS Gifted and Talented page.

items.title: New teacher messaging app, Rooms by Apptegy
items.detail: LCPS launched a two way messaging tool this year. It becomes the only channel for quick notes from teachers, coaches and activity leaders. Invitations went out 2 Sep by text or email and will be resent next week, but you can join without one. Download the LCPS app, allow notifications, pick Watson Mountain in the Feed tab, then use the Rooms or Messaging tab at the bottom. Schoology still holds assignments and ParentVUE still holds grades.

items.title: Video Game Music Club, she is not eligible yet
items.detail: Runs Wednesdays after school, led by Mr. Klinberg. Sixth graders need at least one full year of playing plus permission from Ms. Holowecki, so this is a no for now. Ms. Holowecki is starting a Beginning Strings Club for beginners in the second club season and will send details as the first season closes. Fee carries an extra $15 that pays the professional guest musicians.

items.title: Fall club registration has already closed
items.detail: Registration opened to all families Sunday 6 Sep at 10:00 am and closed Monday 7 Sep. Several clubs sold out during PTO priority access before that. Bus transport was offered for PM sessions only. Year long clubs are separate and the PTO says details are still coming, so that is the next window to watch. Club questions go to clubs@watsonmountainpto.org.

items.title: Math homework runs on Mathspace, most nights
items.detail: Mrs. Reel expects homework after most classes, due the following class period, mostly on Mathspace. Every unit also has a Schoology folder with an agenda listing each day, assignments, completed notes and upcoming test dates. That agenda is the first place to look after an absence.

scans.summary: The overdue cleared. The Strings Sing Me a Story assignment came off the overdue list between Thursday and Friday, so whatever was holding it up is sorted; no score posted with it, which is normal for Ms. Holowecki's in class work. Three new scores, all clean: US History archaeology and sources formative 5 out of 5, Math 9/29 homework 100 out of 100, Math 10/1 homework 100 out of 100. That is five straight hundreds in math since the 71 on quadrilaterals, so the geometry wobble looks like it was the unit, not a habit. The English poster has dropped off the board with no grade yet; Ms. Peyton takes a while on major summatives. One new ask for next week: Mrs. DiPietro wants leftover craft supplies sent in Monday for the solar system models, which start in class on 6 Oct. Monday is already the book fair visit day, so it all goes in the bag together. Nothing overdue and nothing due until the Q1 work on 23 Oct.

The heavy week landed well, with one loose end. Scientific Method major summative came back 100 out of 100, graded within ten minutes of her submitting it, and the Strongest Structure Lab also 100 out of 100. Math 9/18 homework 100 out of 100 and PE week 6 participation 20 out of 20. The loose end is the first overdue of the year: the Strings Sing Me a Story assignment was due Monday at 3:38 pm and is showing two days overdue. That is the one she did in class on Monday without her instrument, so it is probably done and not submitted rather than not done at all. Worth asking her tonight. Field Methods came and went again with no score, third time now for Mrs. Cumberledge. The English poster is due today. Ms. Peyton also announced the Scholastic Book Fair, 5 to 9 Oct, with her English class visiting Monday 5 Oct, so money or an eWallet needs to be sorted that morning.

Sunday night scan ahead of a heavy week. Two things for tomorrow morning: headphones for US History, because Mr. Dickerson is at the district office and the class works independently, and no violin, because Strings is doing a written assignment; it goes back in Wednesday. Three new pieces of work landed. Strings Sing Me a Story is due Monday at 3:38 pm, which is dismissal, so it is classwork. The Strongest Structure Lab write-up is due Tuesday at 11:59 pm if she did not finish it in class. And Mrs. DiPietro's Friday email flagged a practice test in Schoology that counts as a graded formative, open for 15 attempts with the highest score counting, to be done by Tuesday. That last one is the easiest grade available this week and worth more than one pass. The scientific method major summative is Tuesday in class, with the answer key and a Blooket review both posted. The English poster is Wednesday. Both Friday study guides came and went with no score posted, which is normal for study guides. Monday's Field Methods assignment dropped off Schoology on 26 Sep, two days before it is due, same as the last one; worth asking her rather than trusting the portal. Nothing overdue.

Four day catch up scan, and next week is the busiest stretch of the year so far. Four new pieces of work landed: Science scientific method study guide due Friday at 3:30 pm, Math quadrilaterals study guide due Friday at 11:59 pm, Spectrum Field Methods site survey and stratigraphy due Monday at 4:00 pm, and the Science scientific method major summative on Tuesday 29 Sep, with the English poster the day after that. The math one is the one to watch. It is the same quadrilaterals topic as the 71 out of 100 from 14 Sep, and a study guide usually means a unit test behind it. One new score, PE week 5 participation 20 out of 20. The first Field Methods assignment has now vanished from Schoology without a score ever posting, so I have taken it off the board; the new one has the same early 4:00 pm cutoff. Nothing is overdue. The school launched a chocolate fundraiser running to 13 Oct, 80 dollars a box prepaid and non returnable, entirely optional. No posture grade from Strings has appeared yet.

Quiet Saturday. One new score, Science 6H Bubble Lab on the scientific method, 5 out of 5, posted this afternoon. That is two clean science grades in two days. The English compare and contrast tracker has dropped off the upcoming list with nothing overdue, so Friday's formative is done. Mr. Dickerson sent his weekly US History newsletter late Friday night, again as a PDF attachment with an empty email body, this one covering the week of 14 Sep; it cannot be read from here so the pointer is on the board. Nothing else came in. The board now runs to the English poster on 30 Sep, with the Strings posture grade and the calendar vote both landing Tuesday.

Two new scores. Science 6H scientific method knowledge check came back 4.14 out of 5, submitted and graded this morning. Math 7 homework on missing sides and angles from 16 Sep came back 90 out of 100. Put that next to the 71 on quadrilaterals and the 98 on integer operations and a pattern shows: the arithmetic work is clean, the geometry unit is where she drops points. Two homeworks is thin evidence, but it is the same unit twice, so it is worth ten minutes on angle and quadrilateral rules over the long weekend rather than waiting for the unit test. The English compare and contrast tracker was due today and nothing is showing overdue. No new mail from teachers or the district since yesterday.

Two day scan, and Strings carried the day. Ms. Holowecki sent ensemble placements: block 4B puts her in Teal 6 Strings, which means rehearsal 21 Jan and the winter concert 28 Jan with a 6:30 report and 7:00 performance, then rehearsal 18 May and the spring concert 20 May on the same pattern. Those four are now on the board. The same email says every sixth grader gets an instrumental posture grade in class next week and that violins need their own shoulder rest for it, so that is a dated item rather than a standing one. Her Strings block is B day, so Tuesday 22 Sep is the first time it could land. No new grades and nothing overdue. The LCPS Letter was all high school material, PSAT and Credit Through Testing, except that Watson Mountain was named an AMLE School of Distinction.

Two day scan. One new score and it is the one to look at: Math 7 homework on properties of quadrilaterals from 14 Sep came back 71 out of 100, well below everything else this year, which has sat at 98 to 100. It is homework on Mathspace rather than a test, so the useful move is finding which property questions she missed before the unit test lands. Spectrum 6 Field Methods still has no score but has not gone overdue. Removed the FY28 budget ThoughtExchange, which closed yesterday, and added the new strategic plan ThoughtExchange, open to 1 Oct. The Little River board member newsletter had nothing that needs action. No overdue submissions and no new assignments. Next up is the English compare and contrast tracker on Friday and RSM Lesson 2 tomorrow.

Two day scan, pushed late because the previous token stopped authenticating. English 6H loaded a full unit in one go: an in class formative on point of view, conflict and theme today, a compare and contrast tracker due Friday 18 Sep, and the first major summative of the quarter, a one pager poster, due Wednesday 30 Sep. The poster is the thing to plan around. Spectrum 6 Field Methods is marked submitted on the basis that it left the upcoming list after the 4:00 pm cutoff without appearing as overdue, and no score has posted. Added the 2028-29 calendar comment window, which closes with the board vote on 22 Sep. No new grades. Eight Peachjar flyers, all eighth grade or Academies events, nothing that applies.

Two day scan. Two new scores: Math 7 integer operations review from 10 Sep came back 98 out of 100, her first mark under full credit this year, and the PE Week 4 Ultimate Football participation credit posted 20 out of 20 this morning. Added the notice that intramurals and after school clubs start this week, which carries a daily attendance form she fills in herself and a choice between a parent pickup and the two 5:00 pm activity buses. Mr. Dickerson sent his weekly US History update on Sunday with an empty body and everything inside a PDF dated 7 Sep, so it is logged as a pointer rather than pulled apart. No overdue submissions. Spectrum 6 Field Methods is still the only thing due this week, tomorrow at 4:00 pm.
